decision: FAIL for practical Mirror-specific gain; aligned coordinate-compression signal is small in total payload and compute-inefficient
facts: Aligned stratum: Mirror query NRMSE 1.97e-5 at 4,314 B; generic PCA 2.90e-7 at 4,424 B; direct random intrinsic codes 2.80e-7 at 4,510 B.
Mirror total-payload saving vs direct is ~4.3% after charging shared random projection U; task-code-only bytes are 48 B vs 256 B direct (~81% lower).
Mirror takes ~0.915 s and 800 updates / 819,200 task-example presentations; direct intrinsic least-squares takes ~0.00047 s with 1,024 support examples.
Independent stratum: direct coordinates remain ~2.85e-7; Mirror ~0.843 and PCA ~0.614 at similar total payload.
interpretation: The known Givens orbit can be encoded by a shared vector and angles, reducing only the task-specific coordinate state. Once the mandatory shared random projection is included, total storage savings are small. Generic PCA matches quality more closely; Mirror optimization is far slower; unrelated task vectors require private intrinsic coordinates.
hypothesis: Not supported as a practical Mirror application under this protocol. A task-code compression signal exists only for the aligned orbit, while quality/compute Pareto is not improved against direct intrinsic tuning and PCA.
counter_hypothesis: More tasks would amortize the shared projection and could improve total-byte savings; more efficient or analytic angle fitting could reduce compute. These were outside the frozen protocol.
limitations: Synthetic linear regression, random U rather than pretrained model
Aligned teacher generated from exact Givens orbit
Only eight tasks; shared projection dominates total bytes
Independent task stratum shows severe Mirror capacity limitation
No neural finetuning or real-world task evidence
